posts.title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Integrated E-Methanol Production from Biomass Resources
posts.text: Seminar on integrated e-methanol production from first- and second-generation biomass resources, focusing on Aspen Plus process modelling, CO₂ utilization, CAPEX, OPEX, LCOM, and scenario-based techno-economic assessment.

blurbs._help: One-line description shown under each paper, keyed by DOI. Add one when a new paper appears.
blurbs.10.25781/kaust-914yt: Doctoral thesis integrating Aspen Plus process modelling, life cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, uncertainty analysis, and combustion assessment for circular carbon e-fuel pathways from agro-biomass.
blurbs.10.4271/2025-01-0182: First-author study on the techno-economic performance of integrated e-methanol production using first- and second-generation biomass resources.
blurbs.10.1016/j.procir.2025.01.057: First-author regional sustainability assessment of e-methanol production using GLAM-based life cycle impact assessment.
blurbs.10.4271/2024-01-2449: First-author study on sustainable e-methanol production from biomass with enhanced CO₂ utilization.
blurbs.10.1016/j.ijhydene.2025.02.331: Second-author journal article assessing ammonia and hydrogen as alternative fuels for marine internal combustion engines using life cycle assessment.
blurbs.10.4271/2023-24-0067: Second-author technical paper on hydrogen-fueled HCCI engine operation using variable compression ratio strategies.
blurbs.10.1201/9781032687568-23: Second-author publication on the effect of intake temperature on hydrogen HCCI engine combustion and performance characteristics.
blurbs.10.1016/j.energy.2025.138755: Second-author journal article on a Joule cycle-based waste heat recovery approach for marine and heavy-duty vehicle applications.
blurbs.10.1115/icef2025-164599: Second-author conference publication evaluating hydrogen-enriched Euro-6 gasoline in a modified CFR engine, including performance, emissions, and well-to-tank carbon footprint.
blurbs.bb-datepalm: First-author journal article on an integrated bio-/e-methanol pathway from Saudi date palm fruit and residues, combining process modelling, TEA, and LCA.
